commands.review_summary:
Adds a Node script, allowlist, tests, package script, and CI guards invocation to compare GATEWAY_EVENTS with iOS/Android event handlers.

PR surface: Tests +165, Config +2, Other +420. Total +587 across 5 files.

Reproducibility: yes. for the review finding: source inspection shows the PR scans all Android Kotlin files and counts a current non-dispatch node-pair predicate as handled. I did not run repository tests because this review is read-only.
commands.review_followup: - [P2] There is a narrow mechanical repair: tighten Android Kotlin event extraction and add regression coverage, while leaving allowlist policy for maintainer sign-off.

target.title: chore(ci): fail CI when gateway events go unhandled by the mobile apps
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway server→client events (`GATEWAY_EVENTS` in `src/gateway/server-methods-list.ts`) and the event handling in the iOS and Android apps can silently drift apart: a new gateway event ships and no mobile client ever handles it, with no signal anywhere.

Closes #100198

## Why This Change Was Made

There was no machine-checked link between the advertised event catalog and mobile event dispatch. The protocol package only types the event envelope (`event: NonEmptyString`), so nothing fails when a new event name is added server-side. This adds `pnpm check:protocol-coverage`, which derives the event inventory from the gateway catalog, extracts each client's handled events from Swift/Kotlin dispatch sites (switch/when case literals plus `.event == "…"` comparisons), and fails CI for any gateway event a client neither handles nor allowlists. `scripts/protocol-event-coverage.allowlist.json` documents currently-unhandled events per client with a one-line reason each; stale entries (event removed, or now handled) also fail, so the list self-maintains. Sentinel dispatch files fail the check loudly if they move.

## User Impact

No runtime behavior change. Contributors adding a gateway event now get an explicit CI failure until each mobile client either handles it or records an intentional exemption, preventing silently-dropped events in the apps.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/check-protocol-event-coverage.mjs` → `Protocol event coverage OK: 29 gateway events; ios handles 10, allowlists 19; android handles 14, allowlists 15.`
- Negative probe (fake event appended to `GATEWAY_EVENTS`) → exit 1 listing the unhandled event for both clients.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/check-protocol-event-coverage.test.ts` — 8 passed.
- Wired into the CI `guards` check shard in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.
- Codex autoreview on the commit: clean, no accepted findings.

Known limitation (documented in the allowlist): the extractor reads string-literal dispatch only, so iOS `exec.approval.*` handling routed through constants is allowlisted with a reason saying exactly that.
